thread:
Priya: Heads up — AcmeCorp is seeing p95 jump from 120ms -> ~2s and intermittent 429s on their eu-west dedicated pool during autoscale spikes. They also reported a sudden billing increase. Can we triage?
Sam: Which pool + pool config? any tenant id or examples?
Priya: Pool: eu-west-2-dedicated-acme, tenant: acme_prod_42. Happened around their traffic spike at 09:10 UTC. Attaching condensed logs and metrics below.
Priya: ```
09:09:50 request_rate: 1200r/s
09:10:05 autoscaler: scale_up requested -> +2 slots
09:10:10 allocation: fragmented across 2 nodes (frac slices)
09:10:12 client: 429 x27, p95=2.1s
09:10:30 gpu0_sm_util: 95%
09:10:30 gpu1_sm_util: 18%
09:10:40 kv_cache_evictions: spike -> 320
```
Marco: Interesting — allocation shows fractional MIG placement, not co-located cleanly. When autoscaler adds slots it seems to place fractional slices to fit, causing existing tenants to suddenly share a GPU with heavy FP32 workloads.
Olivia: Does the billing spike come from retries/requeues? If requests are retried client-side that could double tokens. Any logs showing retry counts?
Priya: Customer logs show retry loop from SDK (3 retries) for ~400 requests during the incident window. They were getting 429s then backoffs -> extra usage.
Sam: Repro attempt: I ran a load script against a staging pool with similar config and forced a scale event. I see the same pattern: during allocation there is a 20–40s window where p95 jumps and 429s occur.
Sam: Quick repro steps I used:
```
# on load-generator
ab -n 50000 -c 50 https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate?model=acme-8k
# then trigger scale via low cooldown: set autoscaler.min=1 max=8 cooldown=10s
```
Priya: Also saw KV cache thrash and small GC-like stalls in runtime logs: `kv_cache_lock wait 48ms` repeated.
EngRuntime: Hypothesis: fractional-mig packing + immediate traffic causes cold KV caches to be repeatedly evicted when a heavy neighbor lands on the same GPU. Combined with autoscaler aggressively spreading rather than packing, we get burst contention and client retries -> billing bump.
Marco: Agreed. Two levers: 1) increase autoscale cooldown and prefer packing policy to avoid fractional shares during scale events; 2) enforce short isolation window: when allocating new slices, prefer empty GPUs or full-slice allocations for high-tier tenants.
Olivia: Can we propose a temporary mitigation for AcmeCorp while we investigate?
Sam: Workaround I applied in staging for repro: set pool config `pack_policy: pack_by_gpu`, `min_capacity: 2`, `autoscale_cooldown: 60s`. After that, during simulated spikes p95 stayed <200ms and no 429s.
Priya: Can you paste the exact patch so I can propose to customer?
Sam: Patch snippet:```yaml
pool: eu-west-2-dedicated-acme
pack_policy: pack_by_gpu
min_capacity: 2
autoscale:
  cooldown_seconds: 60
  scale_up_step: 2
```
Priya: Sent that to customer; they want a fix that doesn't require increasing committed capacity. Any infra-side quick options?
Marco: Short-term we can enable a placement constraint for their pool to prefer isolated hosts (flag `prefer_isolated_hosts: true`) — this reduces packing efficiency but avoids noisy neighbor spikes. Might require tenant approval for potential cost change.
EngRuntime: Longer term: runtime should delay accepting traffic for new slices until local KV cache is warmed or maintain small-prefetch for cache slots when a new co-tenant arrives. Filing a backlog item.
Priya: Customer also wants root cause writeup and billing remediation because retries caused ~2.3x token usage for the minute.
Olivia: We'll need to correlate request IDs to billing records and advise credits if retries were caused by platform. Please create a billing escalation and assign to account team.
Priya: OK creating internal ticket for billing and dedicated-pool ops.
deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-5982: "AcmeCorp dedicated pool autoscale fragmentation -> latency/429s & billing spike" (https://redwood.atlassian/INF-5982)
Sam: For triage owners: assign to eng-runtime + infra. Quick checklist I recommend: 1) verify allocator packing logs around 09:10 2) confirm MIG slice placement events 3) inspect GPU perf counters for SM throttling 4) correlate client retry IDs -> billing.
Priya: I'll add customer logs to the ticket and share repro script. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Olivia: Follow-up: schedule a 1h postmortem sync tomorrow with infra + runtime + billing. I'll send calendar.
EngRuntime: Noted — starting a small investigation branch for "isolate-warmup".
Priya: Customer accepted the temporary pack_by_gpu workaround for now. Leaving thread open for updates.
